Let

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{j=1}^{100}2^{-\left\lfloor 101k/j\right\rfloor}.
\]

For \(m\ge 1\), let \(N_m\) be the number of pairs \((j,k)\) with \(1\le j\le 100\) such that

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{101k}{j}\right\rfloor=m.
\]

Since all terms are nonnegative,

\[
S=\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}N_m2^{-m}.
\]

For fixed \(m,j\), write

\[
mj=101q+a,\qquad 0\le a\le 100.
\]

Then

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{101k}{j}\right\rfloor=m
\iff
\frac{mj}{101}\le k<\frac{(m+1)j}{101}
\iff
q+\frac{a}{101}\le k<q+\frac{a+j}{101}.
\]

The interval length is \(j/101<1\), so there is at most one integer \(k\).

- If \(a=0\), then \(k=q\) works.
- If \(a>0\), then the only possible integer is \(k=q+1\), which works exactly when
  \[
  a+j>101.
  \]

Now let \(r\equiv m\pmod{101}\), with \(0\le r\le 100\). Since \(101\) is prime, \(a\equiv rj\pmod{101}\).

### Case 1: \(r=0\)

Then \(a=0\) for every \(j\), so

\[
N_m=100.
\]

### Case 2: \(r=100\)

Then \(a\equiv -j\pmod{101}\), so \(a=101-j\). Hence \(a+j=101\) for every \(j\), giving no valid \(k\). Thus

\[
N_m=0.
\]

### Case 3: \(1\le r\le 99\)

Here \(a\neq 0\). Also \(a+j=101\) is impossible, because it would imply \((r+1)j\equiv 0\pmod{101}\), impossible since \(101\nmid r+1\) and \(101\nmid j\).

For \(j=1,2,\dots,100\), define

\[
f(j)=a+j.
\]

The map \(j\mapsto 101-j\) sends \(a\) to \(101-a\), so

\[
f(101-j)=202-f(j).
\]

Thus each pair \(\{j,101-j\}\) contributes exactly one value with \(f(j)>101\). There are \(50\) such pairs, so

\[
N_m=50.
\]

Therefore, as \(m\) runs through the positive integers,

\[
N_{101t+1}=\cdots=N_{101t+99}=50,
\]
\[
N_{101t+100}=0,
\]
\[
N_{101t+101}=100.
\]

Hence

\[
\begin{aligned}
S
&=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}
\left(
50\sum_{r=1}^{99}2^{-(101t+r)}
+100\cdot 2^{-(101t+101)}
\right)\\[2mm]
&=\left(50\sum_{r=1}^{99}2^{-r}+100\cdot 2^{-101}\right)
\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}2^{-101t}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Now

\[
\sum_{r=1}^{99}2^{-r}=1-2^{-99},
\qquad
\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}2^{-101t}=\frac1{1-2^{-101}}.
\]

Thus

\[
\begin{aligned}
S
&=\frac{50(1-2^{-99})+100\cdot 2^{-101}}{1-2^{-101}}\\
&=\frac{50-\frac{50}{2^{99}}+\frac{25}{2^{99}}}{1-\frac1{2^{101}}}\\
&=\frac{50-\frac{25}{2^{99}}}{1-\frac1{2^{101}}}\\
&=\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
